question: Can a two-code registration scheme add garments to the correct wardrobe and category while rejecting guessed, altered, copied, and reused codes?

provenance.disclosure: Code for this pipeline was written with AI assistance (Claude Code, Anthropic) under the author's direction; the author designed the study, reviewed the code and is responsible for the results. Disclose this in the thesis as required by the course's GenAI policy.

design_checks.label: design checks, not research findings (thesis P0430)

deviations: The thesis generates a 500-product test catalogue; this run samples 500 REAL permitted H&M catalogue rows (seeded), which is stronger evidence for category placement.
The public QR payload is the Wearhouse discovery URL with the 128-bit serial, not a GS1 Digital Link: H&M article ids are not GTINs (foundation design D5), so a GS1 link cannot be formed truthfully.
False-claim families run with per-user, per-IP and global admission limits disabled so the limiter cannot mask validation failures; the rate limit is tested separately with production limits.
Category placement is checked against the catalogue facts (product_type_name) and the rule-derived slot (mapping hm-articles@1); products whose group has no slot rule are expected as slot 'unknown'.
